(for Kleene star) that satisfies the following properties:

doc:
**Zhu Shijie's identity** aka hockey-stick identity, version with `range`.
Summing `(i + k).choose k` for `i ∈ [0, n]` gives `(n + k + 1).choose (k + 1)`.

Combinatorial interpretation: `(i + k).choose k` is the number of decompositions of `[0, i)` in
`k + 1` (possibly empty) intervals (this follows from a stars and bars description). In particular,
`(n + k + 1).choose (k + 1)` corresponds to decomposing `[0, n)` into `k + 2` intervals.
By putting away the last interval (of some length `n - i`),
we have to decompose the remaining interval `[0, i)` into `k + 1` intervals, hence the sum.

    have r := [(Lean.Expr.const `Int.natCast_nonneg []).app e'];
    do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.cfg
    have __do_jp : Unit → List Lean.Expr → Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.OmegaM (List Lean.Expr) :=
      fun __r r => pure r
    match __do_lift.splitNatSub, e'.getAppFnArgs with
      | true, (`HSub.hSub, #[head, head_1, head_2, head_3, a, b]) =>
        have r :=
          List.insert (Lean.mkApp2 (Lean.Expr.const `Lean.Omega.Int.ofNat_sub_dichotomy []) a b) r;
        __do_jp () r
      | x, (`Int.natAbs, #[x_1]) =>
        have r := List.insert (Lean.mkApp (Lean.Expr.const `Int.le_natAbs []) x_1) r;
        have r := List.insert (Lean.mkApp (Lean.Expr.const `Lean.Omega.Int.neg_le_natAbs []) x_1) r;
        __do_jp () r
      | x, (`Fin.val, #[n, i]) =>
        have r := List.insert (Lean.mkApp2 (Lean.Expr.const `Fin.isLt []) n i) r;
        __do_jp () r
      | x, (`BitVec.toNat, #[n, x_1]) =>
        have r := List.insert (Lean.mkApp2 (Lean.Expr.const `BitVec.isLt []) n x_1) r;
        __do_jp () r
      | x, x_1 => __do_jp () r
  | (`HDiv.hDiv, #[head, head_1, head_2, head_3, x, k]) =>
    match Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.natCast? k with
    | none => pure ∅
    | some 0 => pure ∅
    | some val =>
      have ne_zero :=
        Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Ne [1]) (Lean.Expr.const `Int []) k (Lean.toExpr 0);
      have pos :=
        Lean.mkApp4 (Lean.Expr.const `LT.lt [0]) (Lean.Expr.const `Int [])
          (Lean.Expr.const `Int.instLTInt []) (Lean.toExpr 0) k;
      do
      let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkDecideProof ne_zero)
      let __do_lift_1 ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkDecideProof pos)
      pure
          [Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Int.mul_ediv_self_le []) x k __do_lift,
            Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Int.lt_mul_ediv_self_add []) x k __do_lift_1]
  | (`HMod.hMod, #[head, head_1, head_2, head_3, x, k]) =>
    match k.getAppFnArgs with
    | (`HPow.hPow, #[head, head_4, head_5, head_6, b, exp]) =>
      match Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.natCast? b with
      | none => pure ∅
      | some 0 => pure ∅
      | some val =>
        have b_pos :=
          Lean.mkApp4 (Lean.Expr.const `LT.lt [0]) (Lean.Expr.const `Int [])
            (Lean.Expr.const `Int.instLTInt []) (Lean.toExpr 0) b;
        do
        let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkDecideProof b_pos)
        have pow_pos : Lean.Expr :=
          Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Lean.Omega.Int.pos_pow_of_pos []) b exp __do_lift
        pure
            [Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Int.emod_nonneg []) x k
                (Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Int.ne_of_gt []) k (Lean.toExpr 0) pow_pos),
              Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Int.emod_lt_of_pos []) x k pow_pos]
    | (`Nat.cast, #[Lean.Expr.const `Int [], head, k']) =>
      match k'.getAppFnArgs with
      | (`HPow.hPow, #[head, head_4, head_5, head_6, b, exp]) =>
        match Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.natCast? b with
        | none => pure ∅
        | some 0 => pure ∅
        | some val =>
          have b_pos :=
            Lean.mkApp4 (Lean.Expr.const `LT.lt [0]) (Lean.Expr.const `Nat [])
              (Lean.Expr.const `instLTNat []) (Lean.toExpr 0) b;
          do

                Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Int.emod_lt_of_pos []) x k cast_pos]

        | (`Nat.cast, #[Lean.Expr.const `Int [], head, x']) =>
          pure [Lean.mkApp2 (Lean.Expr.const `Lean.Omega.Int.emod_ofNat_nonneg []) x' k]

    pure

        Lean.mkApp2 (Lean.Expr.const `Int.min_le_right []) x y]

    pure

doc:
Look up an expression in the atoms, recording it if it has not previously appeared.

Return its index, and, if it is new, a collection of interesting facts about the atom.
* for each new atom `a` of the form `((x : Nat) : Int)`, the fact that `0 ≤ a`
* for each new atom `a` of the form `x / k`, for `k` a positive numeral, the facts that
  `k * a ≤ x < k * a + k`
* for each new atom of the form `((a - b : Nat) : Int)`, the fact:
  `b ≤ a ∧ ((a - b : Nat) : Int) = a - b ∨ a < b ∧ ((a - b : Nat) : Int) = 0`

fun e => do
  let c ← getThe Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.State
  let e ← liftM (Lean.Meta.canon e)
  match c.atoms[e]? with
    | some i => pure (i, none)
    | none =>
      have cls := `omega;
      do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.OmegaM (ℕ × Option (List Lean.Expr)) :=
        fun __r => do
        let facts ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.analyzeAtom e
        let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor `omega
        have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.OmegaM (ℕ × Option (List Lean.Expr)) :=
          fun __r => do
          let i ←
            modifyGetThe Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.State fun c =>
                (c.atoms.size, { atoms := c.atoms.insert e c.atoms.size })
          pure (i, some facts)
        if __do_lift = true then
            if facts.isEmpty = true then __do_jp ()
            else
              have cls := `omega;
              do
              let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
              if __do_lift = true then do
                  let __do_lift ← List.mapM (fun e => liftM (Lean.Meta.inferType e)) facts
                  let __r ←
                    Lean.addTrace cls
                        (Lean.toMessageData "New facts: " ++ Lean.toMessageData __do_lift)
                  __do_jp __r
                else __do_jp ()
          else __do_jp ()
      if __do_lift = true then do
          let __r ← Lean.addTrace cls (Lean.toMessageData "New atom: " ++ Lean.toMessageData e)
          __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ()

doc:
Solve an "easy" equality, i.e. one with a coefficient that is `±1`.

After solving, the variable will have been eliminated from all constraints.

signature.text:
def Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem.solveEasyEquality (p : Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem)
  (c : Lean.Omega.Coeffs) : Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem

value.text:
fun p c =>
  have i := (Lean.Omega.Coeffs.findIdx? (fun x => decide (x.natAbs = 1)) c).getD 0;
  have sign := (c.get i).sign;
  match p.constraints[c]? with
  | some f =>
    have init :=
      { assumptions := p.assumptions, eliminations := (f, i, sign) :: p.eliminations,
        proveFalse?_spec := Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem.solveEasyEquality._proof_1✝ };
    Std.HashMap.fold
      (fun p' coeffs g =>
        match coeffs.get i with
        | 0 => p'.addConstraint g
        | ci =>
          have k := -1 * sign * ci;
          p'.addConstraint (Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Fact.combo k f 1 g).tidy)
      init p.constraints
  | x => p

Walk through the equalities, finding either the first equality with minimal coefficient `±1`,
or otherwise the equality with minimal `(r.minNatAbs, r.maxNatAbs)` (ordered lexicographically).

Returns the coefficients of the equality, along with the value of `minNatAbs`.

Although we don't need to run a termination proof here, it's nevertheless important that we use this
ordering so the algorithm terminates in practice!

  Option (Lean.Omega.Coeffs × ℕ)

value.text:
fun p =>
  Std.HashSet.fold
    (fun x x_1 =>
      match x, x_1 with
      | none, c => some (c, Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.List.minNatAbs c)
      | some (r, m), c =>
        if 2 ≤ m then
          have m' := Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.List.minNatAbs c;
          if
              (decide (m' < m) ||
                  decide (m' = m) &&
                    decide
                      (Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.List.maxNatAbs c <
                        Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.List.maxNatAbs r)) =
                true then
            some (c, m')
          else some (r, m)
        else some (r, m))
    none p.equalities

fun p c =>
  match p.constraints[c]? with
  |
  some
      { coeffs := coeffs, constraint := { lowerBound := some r, upperBound := some r' },
        justification := j } =>
    let m := Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.List.minNatAbs c + 1;
    do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.atomsCoeffs
    have x : Lean.Expr :=
      Lean.mkApp3 (Lean.Expr.const `Lean.Omega.bmod_div_term []) (Lean.toExpr m) (Lean.toExpr c)
        __do_lift
    let __x ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.lookup x
    match __x with
      | (i, facts?) =>
        if hr : r' = r then
          have __do_jp := fun __r =>
            pure
              (p.addConstraint
                {
                  coeffs :=
                    Lean.Omega.bmod_coeffs (Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.List.minNatAbs c + 1) i coeffs,
                  constraint :=
                    Lean.Omega.Constraint.exact
                      (r.bmod (Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.List.minNatAbs c + 1)),
                  justification := Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Justification.bmod m r i (hr ▸ j) });
          match facts? with
          | none => do
            let __r ←
              Lean.throwError
                  (Lean.toMessageData "When solving hard equality, new atom had been seen before!")
            __do_jp __r
          | some facts =>
            if (!facts.isEmpty) = true then do
              let __r ←
                Lean.throwError
                    (Lean.toMessageData
                      "When solving hard equality, there were unexpected new facts!")

            else __do_jp ()

    have data := List.foldl (fun a i => a.push { var := i }) #[] (List.range p.numVars);
    do
    let __s ←
      forIn p.constraints data fun x __s =>
          have data := __s;
          match x with
          | (fst, f@h:{ coeffs := xs, constraint := s, justification := justification }) => do
            let __s ←
              forIn (*...n) data fun i __s =>
                  have data := __s;
                  have x := xs.get i;

                    data.modify i fun d =>
                      if x = 0 then
                        { var := d.var, irrelevant := f :: d.irrelevant,
                          lowerBounds := d.lowerBounds, upperBounds := d.upperBounds,
                          lowerExact := d.lowerExact, upperExact := d.upperExact }
                      else
                        (have s' := Lean.Omega.Constraint.scale x s;
                          have d' := d;
                          have __do_jp := fun __r d' =>
                            have __do_jp := fun __r d' => pure d';
                            if Option.isSome s'.upperBound = true then
                              have d' :=
                                { var := d'.var, irrelevant := d'.irrelevant,
                                  lowerBounds := d'.lowerBounds,
                                  upperBounds := (f, x) :: d'.upperBounds,
                                  lowerExact := d'.lowerExact,
                                  upperExact := d'.upperExact && decide (x.natAbs = 1) };
                              __do_jp () d'
                            else __do_jp () d';
                          if Option.isSome s'.lowerBound = true then
                            have d' :=
                              { var := d'.var, irrelevant := d'.irrelevant,
                                lowerBounds := (f, x) :: d'.lowerBounds,
                                upperBounds := d'.upperBounds,
                                lowerExact := d'.lowerExact && decide (x.natAbs = 1),
                                upperExact := d'.upperExact };
                            __do_jp () d'
                          else __do_jp () d').run;
                  pure (ForInStep.yield data)
            have data : Array Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem.FourierMotzkinData := __s

    have data : Array Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem.FourierMotzkinData := __s

fun p =>
  have data := p.fourierMotzkinData;
  do
  let __x ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem.fourierMotzkinSelect data
  match __x with
    |
    { var := var, irrelevant := irrelevant, lowerBounds := lower, upperBounds := upper,
        lowerExact := lowerExact, upperExact := upperExact } =>
      have r :=
        { assumptions := p.assumptions, eliminations := p.eliminations,
          proveFalse?_spec := Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem.solveEasyEquality._proof_1✝ };
      do
      let __s ←
        forIn irrelevant r fun f __s =>
            have r := __s;
            have r := r.insertConstraint f;
            pure (ForInStep.yield r)
      have r : Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem := __s
      let __s ←
        forIn lower r fun x __s =>
            have r := __s;
            match x with
            | (f, b) => do
              let __s ←
                forIn upper r fun x __s =>
                    have r := __s;
                    match x with
                    | (g, a) =>
                      have r := r.addConstraint (Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Fact.combo a f (-b) g).tidy;
                      pure (ForInStep.yield r)
              have r : Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem := __s
              pure (ForInStep.yield r)
      have r : Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.Problem := __s
      pure r

doc:
Changes the goal to `False`, retaining as much information as possible:

* If the goal is `False`, do nothing.
* If the goal is an implication or a function type, introduce the argument and restart.
  (In particular, if the goal is `x ≠ y`, introduce `x = y`.)
* Otherwise, for a propositional goal `P`, replace it with `¬ ¬ P`
  (attempting to find a `Decidable` instance, but otherwise falling back to working classically)
  and introduce `¬ P`.
* For a non-propositional goal use `False.elim`.

  let __x ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.asLinearCombo y
  match __x with
    | (lc, prf, facts) =>
      have newFacts := List.filter (fun x => decide (p.processedFacts.contains x = false)) facts;
      have cls := `omega;
      do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.OmegaM Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.MetaProblem :=
        fun __r => do
        let __do_lift ←
          (p.problem.addInequality lc.const lc.coeffs
                (some do
                  let __do_lift ← prf
                  liftM (Lean.Meta.mkAppM `le_of_le_of_eq #[h, __do_lift]))).solveEqualities
        pure
            { problem := __do_lift, facts := newFacts ++ p.facts, disjunctions := p.disjunctions,
              processedFacts := p.processedFacts }
      if __do_lift = true then do
          let __r ←
            Lean.addTrace cls

  Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.OmegaM Lean.Expr

value.text:
fun e n =>
  if n < 10 then do
    let atoms ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.atoms
    let tail ←
      liftM
          (Lean.Meta.mkListLit (Lean.Expr.const `Int [])
            (Std.Slice.toArray (Std.Roi.Sliceable.mkSlice atoms n<...*)).toList)
    have lem : Lean.Name := `Lean.Omega.LinearCombo.str (toString "coordinate_eval_" ++ toString n)
    liftM
        (Lean.Meta.mkEqSymm
          (Lean.mkAppN (Lean.Expr.const lem [])
            ((Std.Slice.toArray (Std.Ric.Sliceable.mkSlice atoms *...=n)).push tail)))
  else do
    let atoms ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.atomsCoeffs
    have n : Lean.Expr := Lean.toExpr n
    let eq ←
      liftM
          (Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.mkEqReflWithExpectedType e
            (Lean.mkApp2 (Lean.Expr.const `Lean.Omega.Coeffs.get []) atoms n))
    let __do_lift ←
      liftM
          (Lean.Meta.mkEqSymm
            (Lean.mkApp2 (Lean.Expr.const `Lean.Omega.LinearCombo.coordinate_eval []) n atoms))
    liftM (Lean.Meta.mkEqTrans eq __do_lift)

  Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM Unit

value.text:
fun cfg => do
  Lean.recordExtraModUse `Init.Omega false
  Lean.Elab.Tactic.liftMetaFinishingTactic fun g => do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
      if Lean.Option.get __do_lift Lean.Meta.debug.terminalTacticsAsSorry = true then g.admit
        else do
          let __x ← g.falseOrByContra
          match __x with
            | some g =>
              g.withContext do
                let type ← g.getType
                let g' ← Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprSyntheticOpaqueMVar type
                let __do_lift ← Lean.getLocalHyps
                have hyps : List Lean.Expr := __do_lift.toList
                have cls : Lean.Name := `omega
                let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
                have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM Unit := fun __r => do
                  Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega.omega hyps g'.mvarId! cfg
                  let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.instantiateMVarsProfiling g'
                  let e ← Lean.Meta.mkAuxTheorem type __do_lift true
                  g.assign e
                if __do_lift = true then do
                    let __do_lift ← List.mapM Lean.Meta.inferType hyps
                    let __r ←
                      Lean.addTrace cls
                          (Lean.toMessageData "analyzing " ++ Lean.toMessageData hyps.length ++
                              Lean.toMessageData " hypotheses:\n" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData __do_lift)
                    __do_jp __r
                  else __do_jp ()
            | x => pure ()

{
  set := fun config item =>
    have invalidOption := fun item => item.throwInvalidOption (some `Lean.Meta.Omega.OmegaConfig);
    have item' := item;
    do
    item.addCompletionInfo `Lean.Meta.Omega.OmegaConfig
    if item.isAnonymous = true then invalidOption item
      else
        have root := item.getRootStr;
        have item' := item;
        have item := item.shift;
        if (root == "config") = true then
          if item.isAnonymous = true then
            (fun x item => Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.evalExprWithElab { raw := item.value }) config item'
          else invalidOption item
        else
          if (root == "splitDisjunctions") = true then do
            item'.addConstInfo `Lean.Meta.Omega.OmegaConfig.splitDisjunctions
            if item.isAnonymous = true then
                (fun config item => do
                    let value ← Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.evalBoolItem item
                    pure
                        { splitDisjunctions := value, splitNatSub := config.splitNatSub,
                          splitNatAbs := config.splitNatAbs, splitMinMax := config.splitMinMax })
                  config item'
              else invalidOption item
          else
            if (root == "splitMinMax") = true then do
              item'.addConstInfo `Lean.Meta.Omega.OmegaConfig.splitMinMax
              if item.isAnonymous = true then
                  (fun config item => do
                      let value ← Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.evalBoolItem item
                      pure
                          { splitDisjunctions := config.splitDisjunctions,
                            splitNatSub := config.splitNatSub, splitNatAbs := config.splitNatAbs,
                            splitMinMax := value })
                    config item'
                else invalidOption item
            else
              if (root == "splitNatAbs") = true then do
                item'.addConstInfo `Lean.Meta.Omega.OmegaConfig.splitNatAbs
                if item.isAnonymous = true then
                    (fun config item => do
                        let value ← Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.evalBoolItem item
                        pure
                            { splitDisjunctions := config.splitDisjunctions,
                              splitNatSub := config.splitNatSub, splitNatAbs := value,
                              splitMinMax := config.splitMinMax })
                      config item'
                  else invalidOption item
              else
                if (root == "splitNatSub") = true then do
                  item'.addConstInfo `Lean.Meta.Omega.OmegaConfig.splitNatSub
                  if item.isAnonymous = true then
                      (fun config item => do

doc:
A partially processed `omega` context.

We have:
* a `Problem` representing the integer linear constraints extracted so far, and their proofs
* the unprocessed `facts : List Expr` taken from the local context,
* the unprocessed `disjunctions : List Expr`,
  which will only be split one at a time if we can't otherwise find a contradiction.

We begin with `facts := ← getLocalHyps` and `problem := .trivial`,
and progressively process the facts.

As we process the facts, we may generate additional facts
(e.g. about coercions and integer divisions).
To avoid duplicates, we maintain a `HashSet` of previously processed facts.

doc:
Translates an expression into a `LinearCombo`.
Also returns:
* a proof that this linear combo evaluated at the atoms is equal to the original expression
* a list of new facts which should be recorded:
  * for each new atom `a` of the form `((x : Nat) : Int)`, the fact that `0 ≤ a`
  * for each new atom `a` of the form `x / k`, for `k` a positive numeral, the facts that
    `k * a ≤ x < (k + 1) * a`
  * for each new atom of the form `((a - b : Nat) : Int)`, the fact:
    `b ≤ a ∧ ((a - b : Nat) : Int) = a - b ∨ a < b ∧ ((a - b : Nat) : Int) = 0`

We also transform the expression as we descend into it:
* pushing coercions: `↑(x + y)`, `↑(x * y)`, `↑(x / k)`, `↑(x % k)`, `↑k`
* unfolding `emod`: `x % k` → `x - x / k`

fun only? hyps negGoal => do
  let ctx ← Lean.getLCtx
  forIn hyps PUnit.unit fun expr __s => do
      Mathlib.Tactic.Order.collectFactsImp.processExpr✝ expr
      pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
  Mathlib.Tactic.Order.collectFactsImp.processExpr✝ negGoal
  if (!only?) = true then do
      forIn ctx PUnit.unit fun ldecl __s =>
          if ldecl.isImplementationDetail = true then pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
          else
            have e := ldecl.toExpr;
            if (e == negGoal) = true then pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
            else do
              Mathlib.Tactic.Order.collectFactsImp.processExpr✝ e
              pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      pure ()
    else pure ()

{
  toString := fun fa =>
    match fa with
    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.eq lhs rhs proof =>
      toString "#" ++ toString lhs ++ toString " = #" ++ toString rhs
    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.ne lhs rhs proof =>

    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.le lhs rhs proof =>

    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.nle lhs rhs proof =>
      toString "¬ #" ++ toString lhs ++ toString " ≤ #" ++ toString rhs
    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.lt lhs rhs proof =>
      toString "#" ++ toString lhs ++ toString " < #" ++ toString rhs
    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.nlt lhs rhs proof =>

    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.isTop idx => toString "#" ++ toString idx ++ toString " := ⊤"
    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.isBot idx => toString "#" ++ toString idx ++ toString " := ⊥"
    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.isInf lhs rhs res =>
      toString "#" ++ toString res ++ toString " := #" ++ toString lhs ++ toString " ⊓ #" ++
        toString rhs
    | Mathlib.Tactic.Order.AtomicFact.isSup lhs rhs res =>
      toString "#" ++ toString res ++ toString " := #" ++ toString lhs ++ toString " ⊔ #" ++
        toString rhs }

doc:
`order` solves the main goal if it can be derived from the local hypotheses and the axioms of
`Preorder`, `PartialOrder` or `LinearOrder`. Also supports `⊤`, `⊥` and lattice operations.

This tactic fails if it cannot prove the main goal.

* `order [e₁, ..., eₙ]` uses the terms `e₁`, ... `eₙ` as hypotheses, in addition to the local
  context.
* `order only [e₁, ..., eₙ]` uses only the terms `e₁`, ... `eₙ` as hypotheses (ignoring the local
  context).

doc:
Adds edges to the `≤`-graph using two types of facts:
1. Each fact `¬ (x < y)` allows to add the edge `(x, y)` when `y` is reachable from `x` in the
   graph.
2. Each fact `x ⊔ y = z` allows to add the edge `(z, s)` when `s` is reachable from both `x`
   and `y`.

We repeat the process until no more edges can be added.

`IsScalarTower` instances, as well as `Algebra` corresponding to `RingHom` properties available
as hypotheses.

Example: given `f : A →+* B` and `g : B →+* C`, and `hf : f.FiniteType`, `algebraize [f, g]` will
add the instances `Algebra A B`, `Algebra B C`, and `Algebra.FiniteType A B`.

See the `algebraize` tag for instructions on what properties can be added.

The tactic also comes with a configuration option `properties`. If set to `true` (default), the
tactic searches through the local context for `RingHom` properties that can be converted to
`Algebra` properties. The macro `algebraize_only` calls
`algebraize -properties`,
so in other words it only adds `Algebra` and `IsScalarTower` instances.

doc:
A user attribute that is used to tag `RingHom` properties that can be converted to `Algebra`
properties. Using an (optional) parameter, it will also generate a `Name` of a declaration which
will help the `algebraize` tactic access the corresponding `Algebra` property.

There are two cases for what declaration corresponding to this `Name` can be.

1. An inductive type (i.e. the `Algebra` property itself), in this case it is assumed that the
   `RingHom` and the `Algebra` property are definitionally the same, and the tactic will construct
   the `Algebra` property by giving the `RingHom` property as a term.
2. A lemma (or constructor) proving the `Algebra` property from the `RingHom` property. In this case
   it is assumed that the `RingHom` property is the final argument, and that no other explicit
   argument is needed. The tactic then constructs the `Algebra` property by applying the lemma or
   constructor.

declaration has name `RingHom.Property` and that the corresponding `Algebra` property has name

doc:
This function takes an array of expressions `t`, all of which are assumed to be `RingHom`s,
and searches through the local context to find any additional properties of these `RingHoms`, after
which it tries to add the corresponding `Algebra` properties to the context. It only looks for
properties that have been tagged with the `algebraize` attribute, and uses this tag to find the
corresponding `Algebra` property.

signature.text: def Mathlib.Tactic.Algebraize.addProperties (t : Array Lean.Expr) : Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM Unit

value.text:
fun t =>
  Lean.Elab.Tactic.withMainContext do
    let ctx ← Lean.getLCtx
    ctx.forM fun decl =>
        if decl.isImplementationDetail = true then pure ()
        else do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars decl.type
          match __do_lift.getAppFnArgs with
            | (nm, args) => do
              let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
              match Lean.Attr.algebraizeAttr.getParam? __do_lift nm with
                | some p => do
                  let e ←
                    tryCatch
                        (do
                          let cinfo ← Lean.getConstInfo p
                          ExceptT.run (pure cinfo))
                        fun x => do
                        Lean.logWarning
                            (Lean.toMessageData "Hypothesis " ++ Lean.toMessageData decl.toExpr ++
                                              Lean.toMessageData " has type" ++
                                            Lean.toMessageData
                                              (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr decl.type)) ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData ".\nIts head symbol " ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName nm) ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData
                                        " is (effectively) tagged with `@[algebraize " ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData p ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData "]`, but no constant" ++
                                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofName p)) ++
                              Lean.toMessageData
                                "\nhas been found.\nCheck for missing imports, missing namespaces or typos.")
                        EarlyReturnT.return ()
                  EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun cinfo => do
                      let p' ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkConstWithFreshMVarLevels p)
                      let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.inferType p')
                      let __x ← liftM (Lean.Meta.forallMetaTelescope __do_lift)
                      match __x with
                        | (pargs, fst, snd) =>
                          have tp' := Lean.mkAppN p' pargs;
                          have getValType :=
                            if cinfo.isInductive = true then do
                              pargs[0]!.mvarId!.assignIfDefEq args[0]!
                              pargs[1]!.mvarId!.assignIfDefEq args[1]!
                              let tp ← Lean.instantiateMVars tp'
                              let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isDefEqGuarded decl.type tp
                              if __do_lift = true then pure (some (decl.toExpr, tp)) else pure none
                            else do
                              let e ←
                                tryCatch
                                    (do
                                      let __r ← pargs.back!.mvarId!.assignIfDefEq decl.toExpr
                                      ExceptT.run (pure __r))
                                    fun x => EarlyReturnT.return none
                              EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun __r => do
                                  let val ← Lean.instantiateMVars tp'
                                  let tp ← Lean.Meta.inferType val
                                  pure (some (val, tp));
                          do
                          let __x ← liftM getValType
                          match __x with
                            | some (val, tp) => do
                              let ringHom_args ←
                                Array.filterMapM
                                    (fun x =>
                                      Lean.Meta.liftMetaM do
                                        let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.whnfUntil x `Algebra.toModule
                                        have y : Option Lean.Expr := do
                                          let x ← __do_lift
                                          x.getAppArgs.back?
                                        let __do_lift ←
                                          Lean.Meta.whnfUntil (y.getD x) `RingHom.toAlgebra
                                        let __do_lift_1 ← Lean.Meta.whnfUntil x `RingHom.toModule
                                        pure do
                                            let x ← __do_lift <|> __do_lift_1
                                            x.getAppArgs.back?)
                                    tp.getAppArgs
                              let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.synthInstance? tp)
                              let __do_lift_1 ←
                                Array.allM
                                    (fun z =>
                                      Array.anyM
                                        (fun x =>
                                          Lean.Meta.withoutModifyingMCtx
                                            (liftM (Lean.Meta.isDefEq z x)))
                                        t)
                                    ringHom_args
                              if (__do_lift.isSome || !__do_lift_1) = true then pure ()
                                else
                                  Lean.Elab.Tactic.liftMetaTactic fun mvarid => do
                                    let nm ← Lean.Meta.mkFreshBinderNameForTactic `algebraizeInst
                                    let __x ← mvarid.note nm val (some tp)
                                    match __x with
                                      | (fst, mvar) => pure [mvar]
                            | x => pure ()
                | none => pure ()

Given an expression `f` of type `RingHom A B` where `A` and `B` are commutative semirings,
this function adds the instance `Algebra A B` to the context (if it does not already exist).

This function also requires the type of `f`, given by the parameter `ft`. The reason this is done
(even though `ft` can be inferred from `f`) is to avoid recomputing `ft` in the `algebraize` tactic,
as when `algebraize` calls `addAlgebraInstanceFromRingHom` it has already computed `ft`.

fun f ft =>

    (match ft.getAppFnArgs with
    | (fst, l) => do
      let alg ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkAppOptM `Algebra #[some l[0]!, some l[1]!, none, none])
      let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.synthInstance? alg)
      if __do_lift.isSome = true then pure ()
        else
          Lean.Elab.Tactic.liftMetaTactic fun mvarid => do
            let nm ← Lean.Meta.mkFreshBinderNameForTactic `algInst

            let __x ← mvar.intro1P
            match __x with

            let nm ← Lean.Meta.mkFreshBinderNameForTactic `scalarTowerInst

            let __do_lift_1 ←

            let __do_lift_2 ←
